title: You — general statements

chart.title: You — general statements

intro_examples.text: What can you do on this computer?
intro_examples.continuation: You can play games and do homework.
First, you wash the vegetables. Then you cook them.

chart.note_rule: 'You' can mean 'people in general' — not one specific person.
chart.note_exception: How do you use it? = How does one use it?

tab1_samples: You press the button to turn it on.
You turn the wheel and it moves.
You lift the lid to open it.
You can succeed if you keep trying.

rules.title: 'You' for people in general
rules.subtitle: In English, you doesn't always mean one specific person. It can mean 'people in general'.

transforms.to: You need a battery to use this.
You can find good ideas everywhere.

examples: You need a battery to use this.

rules.title: 'How do you...?' — asking about process
rules.subtitle: Use How do you + verb? to ask how something works in general — not asking one specific person.

transforms.to: How do you use this invention?

transforms.from: How does one make it turn?
transforms.to: How do you make the wheels turn?

examples: How do you make the wheels turn?

rules.title: Giving instructions with 'you'
rules.subtitle: Use you + verb to give step-by-step instructions. Common in recipes and explanations.

transforms.to: First, you put the battery in.

examples: First, you put the battery in. Then you press the button.
You lift your arms and shake your legs.

mixed_samples.text: How do you use that machine? You press the red button.
You need creativity to invent great things.
First, you put the battery in. Then you turn it on.
How do you make the wheels turn?
You can succeed if you keep trying.
How do you solve this problem? You think carefully.
You lift the lid to open the box.
You can find good ideas in everyday life.
How do you use scissors? You hold them like this.
First, you wash the vegetables. Then you cook them.
